title: App Features
text: NHSquicker provides a range of features designed to help users find the most appropriate urgent-care service.

title: App Features
text:
View live wait times
This is the primary function of NHSquicker, enabling users to compare real-time waiting times and choose the most appropriate service for their needs.


Step 1: Enter your postcode






Enter your postcode to find nearby NHS urgent-care services.




Step 2: Choose how to view wait times
Users can view wait times in two ways: a list view or a map view.


List view


View a list of nearby NHS services and compare live waiting times.



Map view


View nearby NHS services on a map to see locations and distances.






Step 3: View service details
Select a service to view more detailed information, including wait times and service status.








Step 4: Get directions
Users can view directions to the selected service, helping them plan their journey.





NHSquicker provides a range of features designed to help users find the most appropriate urgent-care service.


Alternative Services:
The app also provides information for alternative services such as GP and pharmacies:







Health Conditions and Treatments:
The app provides access to trusted information on health conditions and treatments, linking directly to content from the NHS website.
https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/.


Call 111 or 999
NHSquicker allows users to quickly access urgent advice or emergency services when needed.

NHS 111 for urgent medical advice

999 for emergencies only

DIGITAL URGENT CARE DECISION SUPPORT 


NHSquicker is a free app providing real-time waiting time, travel time and service availability information for NHS urgent-care services across Devon, Cornwall and Somerset.


It supports informed decision-making for urgent but non-life-threatening care, helping patients find the most appropriate service while reducing unnecessary pressure on A&E.

DIGITAL URGENT CARE DECISION SUPPORT 


NHSquicker is a free app providing real-time waiting time, travel time and service availability information for NHS urgent-care services across Devon, Cornwall and Somerset.


It supports informed decision-making for urgent but non-life-threatening care, helping patients find the most appropriate service while reducing unnecessary pressure on A&E.

Why the app was developed
A&E services across England have faced increasing pressure, with many departments struggling to meet the national four-hour standard. Research conducted by the University of Exeter in collaboration with NHS partners found that while MIUs and UTCs often met waiting time targets, A&E departments were underperforming due to high demand.
NHSquicker was developed in response to this challenge, using existing NHS data to help patients identify suitable alternatives with shorter waits, reduce overcrowding, and support the wider urgent-care network.


Choose Right Service For urgent, non-life-threatening care


➔


Reduce Overcrowding By choosing the right service for you


➔


Support urgent-care network Across Devon, Cornwall and Somerset

Who the app is for
For the public - People with urgent but non-life-threatening health concerns who need to find appropriate care quickly
For the NHS - NHS Trusts and Integrated Care Boards (ICBs)
- Urgent and emergency care services seeking to better distribute patient demand

Who developed it
NHSquicker is a collaboration between the University of Exeter, NHS organisations across Devon, Cornwall and Somerset, and system integration partners.
The platform has evolved through close collaboration with NHS analysts, clinicians, operational researchers and digital transformation teams, ensuring it meets real-world service needs.

The problem it solves
High attendance at A&E departments for non-emergency conditions leads to long waiting times, overcrowding, and poorer experiences for patients. Many people could be safely treated at MIUs or UTCs but lack awareness of nearby alternatives.
NHSquicker addresses this by providing real-time, practical information that helps people go to the right place, at the right time, reducing avoidable A&E attendances and supporting more efficient use of NHS resources.

title: Evidence & Analytics
text:
Since launching in 2017, NHSquicker has expanded to cover 37 urgent care facilities serving 1.9 million people across Devon, Cornwall and Somerset. Early data shows a positive shift in patient behavior, with reductions in A&E attendance and increased use of MIUs and UTCs. The app also won the Lyn Thomas Impact Medal for demonstrating strong real-world impact and was featured as a REF2021 Impact Case Study.



Unique users graph (17/01/20 - 18/11/25)


The Unique Users graph shows the number of individual user who engaged with the app on a given day. From when we started collecting data (17th Jan 2020) to the present, the number of users per day has increased, and is expected to continue increasing.



Wait time difference split graph (17/01/20 - 19/11/25)


This graph shows summarises user decision-making based on differences in wait times between the closest unit to the user and the unit that the user viewed more options for when viewing wait times on the NHSquicker app. Users most often clicked on units that had shorter wait times than the unit that was closest to them, indicating users are interested in shorter wait times, even if it means travelling further. This highlights the importance of the app for providing real-time wait time information for guiding decisions.





Looking at cases where the nearest unit at the time was an emergency department, the graph shows that from the start of data collection to the present, users selected a unit with a shorter wait 87.2% of the time. The emphasises the usefulness of NHSquicker, and shows its importance in decision making.

What is NHSquicker

NHSquicker is a free app providing live wait times for NHS services in Devon, Cornwall and Somerset. It was created to help people make smarter healthcare choices and reduce unnecessary pressure on the NHS.
